newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BP options active as stock rises.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BP options active as stock rises.

text.p: Traded options in British Petroleum were an active market on Thursday as the underlying stock made a modest gain, dealers said.

One trader sold 1,000 July 700 calls at 50p which may have been a closing deal to take profits. Another was to buy 1,000 October 650 puts at 5p possibly to protect a stockholding in BP if the shares collapse. At the close of business on the stock market, BP shares were up 4p to 744-1/2p.
The share price rise in British Steel prompted one trader to sell 1,000 July 160 puts at 11-1/2p and dealers believed this was to close a bearish position.
British Steel shares closed up 2-1/2p to 155p. The company will announce full year results on June 16.
Elsewhere, in banking group Lloyds TSB 650 September 600 calls were sold at 60p. The underlying shares gained 3-1/2p to 645-1/2p.

In Boots the retailer, one of the larger deals was to buy 250 July 706 puts at 11p. Another was to roll forward a bearish position which involved buying back 200 July 656 calls at 71p and selling 200 October 706 calls at 38p.
And the main deal in Bass was a long straddle.

The deal involved buying 250 October 700 puts and calls in Bass at 30p and 45p each. It will make money if the underlying shares are volatile and at expiry they need to be either below 625p or above 775p.

Over in FTSE 100 index options trading was light and the biggest deal was to buy 1,250 August 4575 puts at 61p which was hedged by buying June FTSE futures at 4730 in a volatility trade. Cash FTSE closed up 32.6 at 4757.4 while June futures were up 34 points at 4772.
